title: ChatStream API bridge: lightweight event surface, resume tokens, and retry contracts
creator: Aria Chen
description: Design and implement a compact, developer-friendly streaming chat surface for the Python SDK that exposes both token/text iterators and structured event streams (delta/role/meta) via a small set of primitives. Provide clear retry/idempotency contracts and resume token semantics so application authors can implement robust backoff/reconnect and reconnect-to-checkpoint workflows without dealing with low-level SSE/HTTP details.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Spike complete: implemented a minimal prototype that converts server event stream into two consumer primitives: .text_iter() (sync/async) and .events() (yields typed Event objects). Verified that switching between sync and async consumers is feasible with a thin wrapper; measure added CPU ~1-3% on microbenchmarks.

2026-03-04 - Decision: surface a single resume_token string per stream (opaque to SDK users) representing an idempotent checkpoint point. The token encodes last-committed event ID + model-kv-offset hint. Pros: simple UX for users; Cons: operator-visible opaqueness — we will provide server-side tooling to decode tokens for debugging.

2026-03-05 - Trade-off discussion with runtime: we considered exposing per-event ack semantics (manual acks) but rejected due to complexity and extra RTT. Instead we will offer best-effort at-least-once delivery with de-duplication guidance (event_id and timestamps).
2026-03-06 - Review notes from PM (Rita Singh): emphasize examples for resumable chat UIs and long-running agents. Add cookbook showing "resume after transient network blip" pattern.

2026-03-08 - Design feedback from Security (Liam O'Neal): resume tokens must not contain PII or unencrypted payload — runtime will HMAC + optional KMS encryption. Marked security_review_required = true for runtime changes; SDK surface unchanged.

2026-03-09 - Engineering notes: retries policy for streaming connect attempts: exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts 8, escalate to non-streaming (polling) fallback after repeated failures. Added telemetry hooks: stream_connect_attempt, resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure.

2026-03-11 - Integration test plan: create harness that simulates mid-stream disconnects at token boundaries and verifies that client resumes without duplicate display for idempotent events (test uses deterministic event ids).
2026-03-12 - PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/2447 (prototype API + tests). TODO: address async cancellation semantics and GC of background tasks before merge.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes ChatStream.text_iter() and ChatStream.events() in both sync and async flavors
SDK supports resume token passed into ChatStream.resume(token=...) and performs deterministic reconnection attempts
Retry policy and example cookbook available in docs/ and README with recommended backoff and fallback to non-streaming mode
Unit/integration tests simulate disconnects and validate no visible duplicate tokens/text for idempotent events
Telemetry events emitted for connect/resume attempts that match telemetry contract (docs link in attachments)
technical_notes: We intentionally keep the surface minimal: two orthogonal primitives (text iterator, event iterator). Event objects are small typed records: {event_id, type, delta, role, meta}. Consumers that need strict exactly-once semantics should use server-side persisted messages with application-level dedupe using event_id. Resume tokens are opaque base64(HMAC(version|last_event_id|kv_offset|ts)).
recommended_retry_policy: Connect retries: exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max 8 attempts, jitter randomized, on repeated failure fall back to polling endpoint (non-streaming). Resume attempts: attempt immediate resume up to 3 times with short backoff, then escalate to fresh session with server-side rewind to last known stable checkpoint.
example_snippet:
# sync example
from redwood import ChatClient
client = ChatClient()
stream = client.chat_stream(model="rwd-gpt-3.5", messages=conversation)
for chunk in stream.text_iter():
    # chunk is incremental text (may be partial token)
    print(chunk, end="")

# events() gives typed events (useful for structured signals)
for ev in stream.events():
    if ev['type']== 'function_call':
        handle_function_call(ev['meta'])
    elif ev['type']== 'final':
        save_message(ev['delta'])

# resume example (after transient network failure)
resume_token = last_seen_resume_token
stream2 = client.chat_stream(model="rwd-gpt-3.5", messages=conversation, resume=resume_token)
for text in stream2.text_iter():
    process(text)
open_questions: 1) Do we expose resume token decoding helpers in the SDK for debugging? 2) Should we add an explicit 'ack' primitive for high-throughput agent workflows that must avoid duplicates? 3) How to unify error taxonomy across sync/async (we currently map low-level EOF/Cancel to StreamInterrupted and raise same typed exception in both flavors).
next_steps: Address async cancellation GC (race where background thread remains after task cancelled), finalize telemetry event names, implement optional user callback hooks for on_resume/on_disconnect, add cookbooks and examples to docs site.
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the proposed resume token format and security note — runtime will provide HMAC+optional KMS wrap. Also review the integration tests for flaky timing assumptions (we may need to make tests deterministic by injecting clock).
